 Weather Flood Warning: Joburg Residents Warned To Stay Alert
 Staff Writer 
 Published: November 18, 2026 
 Share 
 3 Min Read 
 Heavy rains resulted in Klipspruit being flooded, and water spilled over into the streets of Soweto, endangering residents 
 SHARE 
 Johannesburg – Residents of the City of Johannesburg have been urged to remain on high alert and exercise extreme caution following significant flooding in Region C, Region D (Greater Soweto), Region E and Region G.
 “Rising water levels have affected several roads, public transport infrastructure and residential properties, creating potentially dangerous conditions for motorists, pedestrians and public transport users,” the Government Communication and Information System (GCIS) warned.
 An 11-year-old girl was reportedly swept away by floodwaters in Dobsonville Ext 3. She remains missing.
 In another incident, a nine-year-old boy was reportedly swept away by Klipspruit’s raging waters in Soweto.
 The Johannesburg Roads Agency (JRA) has deployed operational teams to affected areas.
 “Teams are clearing debris from stormwater drains, assessing the safety of roads and bridges, and monitoring conditions to identify and respond to infrastructure-related risks,” GCIS said.
 “These operations will continue as weather conditions and water levels evolve.”
 Government urges residents to prioritise their safety and take precautions:
• Never attempt to drive or walk through flooded roads. Even shallow-looking water can conceal potholes, open manholes, damaged road surfaces or strong currents.
• Do not attempt to cross flooded bridges, low-lying roads, underpasses or overflowing streams. Turn around and find an alternative route.
• Motorists must reduce their speed, maintain a safe following distance, switch on headlights where visibility is poor and avoid sudden braking.
• Pedestrians should avoid walking through floodwater, particularly near stormwater channels, rivers and drainage systems.
• Keep children away from flooded areas, rivers, streams and stormwater drains.
 “Residents are also encouraged to check on vulnerable neighbours, particularly older persons, persons with disabilities and households in flood-prone communities,” GCIS said.
 Report flooded roads, damaged bridges, blocked stormwater drains, fallen trees obstructing roadways and other road infrastructure emergencies through the following channels:
• City of Johannesburg Call Centre (24/7): 0860 562 874
• JRA Email Hotline: hotline@jra.org.za
• Life-threatening emergencies and rescue services: 10177 or 112 (from a cellphone)
• JMPD: 011 375 5911
• Social media updates: @MyJRA on X (formerly Twitter) and Johannesburg Roads Agency on Facebook.
 Meanwhile, the South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued an extended weather forecast for Thursday and Friday, 19-20 November 2026.
 SAWS predicts partly cloudy and hot to very hot weather, with isolated showers and thundershowers, becoming scattered in places in the east on Friday
